findings.claim: `ctx.clearCache()` may not exist on the Vitest instance, causing a runtime `TypeError: ctx.clearCache is not a function` when `--clearCache` is passed.
findings.rationale: The diff only shows the call site being renamed from `experimental_clearCache` to `clearCache`. If the corresponding method on the `Vitest` class (and its public type declarations / `.d.ts`) was not renamed or aliased in the same change, this call resolves to `undefined` and throws at runtime on the exact CLI path it is meant to serve. Worth confirming the class-side rename landed; I cannot see the class definition in this hunk, so confidence is moderate.

findings.claim: Dropping the `experimental_` prefix is a public API break for external callers that still invoke `experimental_clearCache()`.
findings.rationale: `experimental_clearCache` was an exported/public method on the Vitest node API, not internal-only. If the old name was removed rather than kept as a deprecated alias, any programmatic consumer calling it breaks without a deprecation cycle. Also, promoting an experimental API to stable implies the behavior/signature is now committed to; that should be intentional and documented. Confidence moderate — the removal itself is outside this hunk.

findings.claim: Potential name collision: `clearCache` is also the name of the config flag (`ctx.config.clearCache`) and may shadow or conflict with an existing differently-behaving method of the same name.
findings.rationale: Renaming to a generic `clearCache` increases the chance of colliding with a pre-existing member (e.g. an internal cache-clearing helper used during watch-mode reruns) that has different semantics. If such a member exists, the rename silently overrides it and `--clearCache` would perform the wrong operation. Low-to-moderate confidence; needs a grep of the Vitest class for an existing `clearCache` member.
